audit.whatIsWrong: THE WHOLE FULL LAYER TRACKS A FABRICATED ABILITY. 'Repeating Dashes' is not an Ambessa ability — it appears in tldr, winCon, enemyWin, ahead, loading, focus.text, breakdown.mid, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.spikes, breakdown.difficulty, dosFull[0], dosFull[2], report[5], report[9], report[10] and report[13]. Her real kit is Drakehound's Step (P), Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam (Q), Repudiation (W), Lacerate (E), Public Execution (R).
audit.why: The decisive interactions were never stated. Repudiation gives her a shield, braces, and then deals INCREASED damage in proportion to the non-minion damage it blocked — so opening your burst into the brace both loses the burst and feeds her damage. Drakehound's Step is the tell: entering a move or attack command during a cast makes her dash and empowers her next attack with bonus range and damage, so the dash is the cue to step back, not the ability cast. Public Execution suppresses on arrival, which is what breaks a Slicing Maelstrom channel.
audit.corrected: Every 'Repeating Dashes' string replaced with the real ability that actually does the job in that sentence; report[5].t now states the Repudiation brace rule, dontsFull[0].d the Drakehound's Step tell, and enemyWin the suppression.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers in the full layer, and no statement of the ultimate race.
audit.why: Repudiation is 18/17/16/15/14, Lacerate 13/12/11/10/9, Cunning Sweep 14/13/12/11/10, Public Execution 130/115/100. Kennen's Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120 — lower than her rank-1 130, so at level 6 Kennen gets the second ultimate first.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt with the real numbers and the 120-vs-130 race stated; dosFull[0].d, breakdown.mid, breakdown.difficulty and report[9].t now carry the 18s Repudiation.

notes: Biggest find in this slice so far: the entire Kennen-side full layer tracked 'Repeating Dashes', an ability Ambessa does not have — 16 separate strings. All replaced with the real ability that does the job in each sentence. Ambessa's Public Execution carries a derived 'heal' flag that Riot's own description does not support (blink, suppress, slam, damage, stun — no healing), so no new healing claim was made; the pre-existing anti-heal advice in report[8].t and breakdown.late was left untouched rather than removed, and is listed as unverified. Public Execution's derived 'grounding' flag is likewise absent from Riot's text and was not asserted. The content layer is accurate and was left alone; the level chart already agrees across both layers and with the packet, so no chart edits.
